A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sign lock-in study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original sign-compressibility measurements, training-trajectory analyses, controlled interventions, and compression experiments, including the appendix benchmarks.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds model-scale, Pythia-1B, ImageNet, AdamW-update, and CNN analyses in Appendix E.1.

M1.justification: The template, gap initialization, log-barrier, hard projection, and magnitude-SVD pipeline already appear in v1, including Appendix E.3. The limited procedural addition is NormalFloat factor quantization for the new ImageNet experiment; v2 retains the original symmetric-uniform quantization pipeline.

E1.justification: V2 adds end-to-end ImageNet image-classification compression with ResNet, substantially extending evaluation beyond v1's MNIST and language/text-classification experiments. CharLM, Text8-Char, DBPedia14, and their distillation variants were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The corresponding compression comparisons retain raw-weight SVD, HashedNets, OneBit, magnitude pruning, WANDA, and QAT. The ImageNet experiment extends the existing vanilla-SVD comparison to another benchmark; the rewritten OneBit citation does not identify a new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 introduces a 0.3M–512M model sweep with best-versus-final validation measurements, analysis of Pythia-1B trained on 300B tokens, and ImageNet Top-5 evaluation over 0.5–4 bits per weight using NormalFloat factors. These are added settings, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test the performance cost of rank-2 templates across scale, overfitting, geometric flip distributions in long-trained Pythia and a CNN, and empirical AdamW update bounds. Figure 2(a) and Table 7 also add raw-weight approximation errors to investigate the sign component's role in compression difficulty.

E5.justification: Retained experiments still use three-seed mean±standard-deviation reporting and the same zero-inflated geometric fitting procedure. The new tables do not establish additional repetitions, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty estimation; update percentiles describe an added analysis rather than estimation uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 add substantial numerical evidence. Table 4 reports 84.016% zero effective flips for Pythia-1B. The new ImageNet comparison reports template versus vanilla-SVD Top-5 accuracy of 42.0% versus 0.5% at 1 bit, but 81.3% versus 83.8% at 4 bits. These are newly reported outcomes; v1's six compression panels are retained as v2 Figures 8 and 22.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, geometric-tail theorem, and Appendix D proofs are retained. The repaired main-text flip-ratio expression matches the mismatch metric already correctly defined in v1 Appendix C.3.6, rather than introducing new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement shift emphasis from flip suppression to a from-scratch sign-template method that avoids the one-bit wall. The conclusion replaces broader suggestions about sparsity, attention-head selection, and routing with post-training compression as future work. The central empirical and theoretical claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations that template-related performance costs diminish with scale, template training reduces overfitting, and observed AdamW updates support the bounded-update premise. It also explicitly limits the compression method to training from scratch and explains why the results do not establish conversion of arbitrary pretrained checkpoints.

D1.justification: The new appendix supplies limited setup information, including Pythia-1B's 300B-token training budget, model sizes, NormalFloat factor quantization, and the update-check threshold. Existing hardware/software, projection, and bit-accounting details are retained. Detailed recipes for the added experiments and new code/data access information are not supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit distinction from already-cited DoReFa-Net and TTQ: preserving a regenerable sign prior reallocates storage to magnitudes, whereas those methods store learned discrete states. Moving related work and correcting bibliographic metadata do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes Section 4 around the complete from-scratch compression pipeline and integrates previously appendix-only compression evidence into the main narrative. It rewrites the abstract, contribution framing, conclusion, and limitations, consolidates related work in Appendix B, and reorganizes Appendix E.

P2.justification: V2 adds the explanatory sign-template Figure 5 and seven empirical tables, and redraws Figure 2(a) with raw-weight curves and revised legends. V1's six-panel Figure 20 is split between main-text Figure 8 and appendix Figure 22. Most other plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the existing compression contribution easier to understand and clearly states its from-scratch applicability. New scale, ImageNet, and optimizer analyses broaden supporting evidence. These gains are limited by sparse protocols and uncertainty reporting for the additions, and Table 3's inconsistency: the 0.3M model's final PPL of 5.56 is below its stated best PPL of 5.61.
